meta.title: Daily contest: top picks, weekly winners · Fizlet
meta.description: The Fizlet Daily contest: up to 40 entries a day, the top 1 to 5 picked, a weekly and a monthly winner; over 10,240 B live can't win.

head.eyebrow: PICKED EACH DAY · WON EACH WEEK AND MONTH
head.lead: Tiny examples, made every day. It's how we test the engine. We turned it into a contest. Up to 40 entries a day. The top 1 to 5 of each day are picked, and all of them are posted at the end of the week. Then a weekly winner, and a monthly winner. The voters: the studio crew, Frame Zero, DJ Mempool, Hex Hazel, Quill, Pip and Chris Cooley. When a day has too few entries, the team backfills it with its own pieces. Over 10,240 B live, a piece goes in the Hi-Fi lane, with a weekly winner of its own. See the pieces on Daily.

week.label: THEME
week.brief: No theme was set this week: any prompt counts, and the week's approved dailies are its entries.

lanes.title: This week's pieces so far, smallest first

pieces.label: Grid duel
pieces.prompt: “two light-cycles duel on a neon grid laid over the page: tap to turn, their walls of light crash into the page's real elements and each other, a crash breaks into pixels; every round sudden death against a new rival AI”

pieces.label: Grab-O-Tron
pieces.prompt: “a wood-grain claw machine whose prizes are the page's letters: tap to drop the claw; half the time it fumbles the block back onto the pile, and a win spits out tickets”

pieces.label: the bubble-top
pieces.prompt: “a space-age bubble-top car zips past houses on stilts above the clouds, puffing smoke rings: tap to swerve, honk or bump a house”

pieces.label: Spin it back
pieces.prompt: “a caped flier circles the globe until the world spins backwards and the page rewinds”

badge.what: Spin it back, its live chunk

pieces.label: Stack it
pieces.prompt: “the bricks, by their real names and measured sizes, scatter over the stage, stack up and morph into an app; then you stack your own, press FINISHED and your app gets its stars”

pieces.label: rush hour
pieces.prompt: “sky-city rush hour: flying bubble cars weave between floating platforms; tap to drop a traffic beacon and cause a comic pile-up”

pieces.label: Hill war
pieces.prompt: “two critters on two hills take turns: pick a weapon chip (ball, cluster, bouncy, mega bomb), tap where it should land, mind the wind; every blast chunks the hill and knocks the sign's words off”

pieces.label: Jack in
pieces.prompt: “a netrunner jacks into a corp's page behind rain-soaked glass: its real elements are ICE nodes, taps fire hack packets that ricochet off them, a breach glitches only the text it hits; trip the alarm and black ICE hunts your cursor”

pieces.label: Gecko climbs the page
pieces.prompt: “a gecko-suited hero climbs the page and swings between its blocks on a grappling line”

badge.what: Gecko climbs the page, its live chunk

pieces.label: Pricing war
pieces.prompt: “two pricing plans are forts built from their own page blocks: tap to fire (one tap a fast shell, two a big slow bomb), the other plan fires back, and every hit crumbles real blocks and knocks letters out”

pieces.label: WALKIES
pieces.prompt: “a space-age pup on a moving walkway: tap to go faster until it flings him across the page”

pieces.label: Patch slash
pieces.prompt: “pumpkins, gourds and the odd black bomb pumpkin toss up over a harvest-fair flyer; swipe to slice: halves fly, pulp splats stick to the letters, a bomb blows a word apart, combos count”

pieces.label: Stone strike
pieces.prompt: “a stone-age bowler twirls on tiptoe and rolls a stone ball where you click, into the page's words set up as ten pins; they scatter and knock each other over, all ten is a strike, a double click throws a hooking twister, and a pterosaur pinsetter sets the words back”

pieces.label: Foot brake
pieces.prompt: “a stone-age dad runs his foot-powered stone car down Main Street; click and he brakes with his heels, the car skids in a cloud of dust and its load of rocks flies on into the billboard's letters; a double click floors it, and the speed bump is a page element he hops”

lanes.title: This week's Hi-Fi pieces, their own lane

pieces.label: GOOD BOY
pieces.prompt: “a space-age pup rolls over for a belly rub: scratch him till he floats, too much and he gets the zoomies”

pieces.label: Rock drop
pieces.prompt: “a long-neck crane dino at the stone-age quarry drops boulders where you click; they crack the stone letter blocks, knock them out of the stack and bounce, and a double click hauls the big one that shakes the page”

pieces.label: CitySmash
pieces.prompt: “a giant cyber ape against a tabletop city block, side-on: dress him first (fur colour and pattern, a brow, a crest or tusks, a cyber arm, a visor, a chest plate, tail spikes, a neon trim), then jump at the buildings' side walls, hang on and punch the windows next to you until each building shakes and pancakes floor by floor; live wires and neon signs shock you off, people at the windows are snacks, soldiers, a tank and a helicopter fight back; two rival giants of our own (a crystal crab-beast and a tentacle blob) wreck the same block, and a second player can take one”

rules.title: Rules
items: Up to 40 entries a day. Anyone can enter: a prompt, or a piece of your own. A week runs Monday to Sunday, UTC.
The top 1 to 5 of each day are picked by the voters: the studio crew, Frame Zero, DJ Mempool, Hex Hazel, Quill, Pip and Chris Cooley.
All the picks are posted at the end of the week on Daily, each approved by the owner before it goes live. Archived pieces don't enter.
One weekly winner, from that week's picks, then one monthly winner from the month's weekly winners. Winners wear a Winner badge on Daily and on their maker's page.
Not enough entries? The team backfills the day with its own pieces, credited to whoever made them.
Small wins. Size decides, not the prompt: to win, a piece's live code is 10 KB gzip or less (10,240 B, measured at build). The week's smallest piece that can win is marked Smallest.

Hi-Fi has its own lane. Bigger, high-fidelity pieces (dioramas, 2.5D, full mini-games, heroes over the cap) are marked Hi-Fi and compete only with each other, for their own weekly winner. Every piece over the cap is Hi-Fi; a Hi-Fi piece can't win the micro week, and a micro can't win Hi-Fi.
Every piece keeps the contract: still once it settles, asleep off screen, and the page comes back.

enter.title: How to enter
enter.intro: Entries come in on GitHub for now.
steps: Open an issue from the prefilled form below: the week is in the title; add your prompt and, if you have them, a link to your code and its size. If the voters pick it, you are credited.
Or open a pull request that adds your piece to site/gallery/. The build measures it; over 10 KB it goes in the Hi-Fi lane ("lane": "hifi" on its entry).

winners.label: Tilt Maze
winners.prompt: “the classic wooden labyrinth box on a tabletop diorama: tilt the board (drag, the arrows, or the phone itself after a permission key) to roll a steel ball along a numbered line past the holes; fall in one and it drops through and comes back to the start; real rolling physics with gravity from the tilt, friction, wall bounces, the ball's shadow and highlight, the board leaning on its frame and the knobs turning with it; three boards of rising difficulty, a timer and a best time”

winners.label: Never Loses
winners.prompt: “tic-tac-toe against a smug bot that plays perfectly; beside the board its source grows one more nested if with every move until the ladder runs off the panel, and play again only nests it deeper”

winners.label: Mirror Maze
winners.prompt: “five little laser puzzles on a tabletop diorama: a tray on a table with a laser emitter, stone posts, two to four mirrors you tap to turn 45 degrees and later a glass splitter that sends the light two ways; light every crystal, each chimes as the beam reaches it, and the next board slides in; a moves counter and a par for every board”

winners.label: ILOVEYOU
winners.prompt: “Outbreak, act 1 (2000): the love letter opens itself and mails a copy to every contact in the address book, and every contact who opens it mails it on; tap a letter in flight to delete it, and its blast shreds the letters beside it”

winners.label: Oodles o' Moles
winners.prompt: “a midway poster with a hole punched in every O and a mole in each: bonk them with the mallet for tickets, a hard hat takes two, and bonking the one with the bomb blows the letters about”
